# Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#clinical-conversational-user-study)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.00605v1) · arXiv v1; PDF dated 31 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 35 PDF pages: main Sections 1-4, availability and ethics, Appendices A-C, all questionnaire items and 45 fixed questions, statistical formulas, model selection and post-study correctness analysis. Visually inspected interface screenshot on PDF page 27.

## Research question

Clinical SQL benchmark accuracy alone cannot show whether practitioners can express information needs, resolve misunderstandings or trust an interface appropriately.

## Method

Fourteen physicians compare single-turn and conversational GPT-5.4 interfaces over the 100-patient MIMIC-IV Demo in a randomized-order, counterbalanced within-subject study. Fixed selected questions precede free exploration; questionnaires measure usability, acceptance and perceived trust.

## Evaluation

SUS and UTAUT comparisons use paired tests. Dialogue coding pools 425 user turns from 21 professionals including two pilots with changing models/procedures. A separate post-study review judges 186 evaluable SQL-generating turns from 57 main-study conversational sessions against gold answers or complete dialogue context.

## What the results support

Mean SUS rises from 68.2 to 85.9. Free questions prompt clarification on 40/161 conversational turns versus 1/56 predefined turns; 27/42 episodes involve clinical or EHR knowledge. Study designers judge 134/186 conversational outputs correct, with errors involving entity matching, population/aggregation and cross-turn propagation.

## Limits and qualifications

Fourteen main participants, one small demo database and strong prior conversational-AI familiarity limit generalization. Trigger frequency measures this agent’s behavior rather than independently adjudicated ambiguity prevalence. Pooled pilots differ from the main protocol; post-study correctness is not a matched interface accuracy comparison. Trust remains self-reported.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Adds rare practitioner evidence and concrete ambiguity categories while exposing a gap between satisfaction and verified conversational correctness.
